conviction_note: No company-level number the market has not seen. The FY comp guide needs about -1% in H2 against an easy Q4 lap, the tariff refund and buybacks support EPS, and a 13%-of-shares short with 6 of 7 up reactions argues for a small up-lean. Against that, mortgage rates rose to 7.3% (highest since 2023), Lowe's cut and Sherwin-Williams' 'muted into 2027' put the Q4 trend and guide at risk. Findings sum +0.7; scaled +0.36 = (2*0.53-1)*6.0. abs_move is set below the 7.49 option figure because of the 41% ATM spread and a 3.89 median history, and above that median because the full-year comp/revenue guide is likely to move.
bar: Q3 adj EPS $0.58 on revenue ~$1.22bn (Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FND/earnings-forecasts and Earnings Whispers https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FND/21195, which agree; whisper $0.60). Company FY2026 guide (8-K 2026-07-30, https://ir.flooranddecor.com/sec-filings/content/0001628280-26-051055/fnd-20260625x8kxex991.htm): comps -4% to flat, net sales $4.77-4.99bn, adj EPS $1.88-2.13, adj EBITDA $550-585m, with the 53rd week included. Q3-to-date comp at the Q2 call was -2.2%. Q3 2025 lap: comp -1.2%, sales $1,179.5m. Consensus FY $1.94 / $4.84bn sits in the lower half of the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 13,797,528 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 13.0% of shares outstanding, 5.06 days to cover; 13.90m at 09-30 and 14.5m at 07-31, so slowly falling (https://equibles.com/stocks/fnd/shortinterest). Skew +14.49 vol points (downside paid); put/call OI ratio 34.9 in the baseline. The stock fell from $62.30 (insider sale price on 2026-08-07) to about $45 on 2026-10-21 (-23% over three months per Earnings Whispers), then bounced to $49.61 (20-day run-up +7.8%). Reaction history: 6 of 7 up, including +4.48% after a Q1 2026 EPS miss and guide cut.

findings.finding: Housing financing worsened inside and after the quarter. The Freddie Mac 30-year rate was 7.28% on 2026-10-01 (highest since Nov 2023) and 7.32% on 2026-10-22, against 6.86% in September and 6.35% a year earlier. September existing-home sales were 3.99m SAAR, down year over year in all regions, and builder confidence hit a 14-year low. The FY comp guide's midpoint (-2%), which management said it was 'highly confident' of, needs H2 at roughly -1%. That puts the Q4 commentary, and the comp and revenue guide, at risk of a cut to the lower half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (2026-04-30): EPS missed and the FY guide was lowered, yet the stock rose +4.48%. Q3 2025 (2025-10-30): comp -1.2% near the low end, stock -3.89%. Guide cuts have not reliably been sold on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock fell about 23% from August to Oct 21 while rates rose, and the skew pays for downside. What is not priced is how the company translates rates into its Q4 comp and guide. If the market expected a cut, the stock would not have bounced about 10% in the week before the print.
findings.independence: Proxy, macro to company. Same direction: NAR September existing-home sales via Mortgage News Daily (https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com/news/10162026-existing-home-sales-nar-inventory-prices-appr, 2026-10-16), and new-home sales with the builder-confidence low (https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/823525, 2026-10-27). FND has not confirmed any transmission since its July call.

findings.finding: Sherwin-Williams' Q3 release (2026-10-27) said 'customer sentiment and the leading indicators we track point to muted demand over the remainder of the year and into 2027' and cited soft North American DIY demand in Consumer Brands. In the same release, residential repaint (pro) grew mid-single digits and Paint Stores same-store sales rose +3.9%. For FND, which is about 55% pro, the read is mixed with a negative lean on the outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No FND-specific history on peer read-throughs; FND's guidance-driven moves have been +/-4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Two days old and a different category (paint). FND rose into the print after it, so the 'muted into 2027' read has not visibly been applied to FND.
findings.independence: Peer proxy. The pro-strength half of this release points the other way, which is why the size is small.

findings.finding: Home Depot Q2 FY26 (quarter ended 2026-08-02, overlapping FND's July): US comp +1.3%, flooring among 13 of 16 departments with positive comps, tickets over $1,000 +2.4%, FY guide reaffirmed (comps flat to +2%). This suggests the flooring category held up through FND's weak early-July stretch.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since August, so mostly priced. It bears on Q3 comp versus the -2.2% QTD figure, which previews still anchor on.
findings.independence: Separate document from Lowe's (next finding), which points the other way.

findings.finding: Lowe's Q2 2026 (2026-08-19): comp +0.2%, weak discretionary DIY, and the FY comp outlook cut to flat from flat to +2%. This is a home-improvement peer that cut after FND last spoke on 2026-07-30.
findings.why_not_priced: Ten weeks old and part of the slide FND took from $62 to $45, so largely priced. Kept small for the guide read-through.
findings.independence: Pairs with the Home Depot finding, which offsets it.

findings.finding: Management's own comp math favours holding the FY guide. H1 comp was -2.9% (Q1 -3.7%, Q2 -2.1%), so the -2% midpoint needs H2 at about -1.1%. Q4 laps a -4.8% comp against Q3's -1.2% lap, and Q4 carries the 53rd week (~$65m sales, ~$0.08 EPS). Late July and early August returned to the May/June run rate (-1.3%/-0.3%), and management said it had 'a high level of confidence' in the midpoint. A Q3 comp near -2% therefore still leaves a path to the midpoint on an easy Q4 compare.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-30): comps improved and the EPS guide was raised, stock +4.10%. Q4 2025 (2026-02-19): +4.34%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews frame the print as 'whether comps improve from -2.2%' (Earnings Whispers, 2026-10-21) and do not do the Q4 lap arithmetic. A market pricing a held guide would not carry +14.5 points of put skew into a name already 35% off its high.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 comp -4.8% per Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FND/21195); Q3 2025 comp -1.2% per the 2025-10-30 8-K (https://ir.flooranddecor.com/sec-filings/content/0001628280-25-047536/fnd-20250925x8kxex991.htm). Shares the call transcript with the tariff-refund finding below, but rests on a different number.

findings.finding: EPS support beyond comps: about $22m of tariff refunds booked in inventory flows through H2 COGS (part of Q3), $87m of refund cash came in after Q2, and buybacks continue ($65.7m in Q2, $334m authorization left). Q3 adjusted EPS is likely at or above the $0.58 consensus, and the whisper is $0.60. All of this sits inside the company's adjusted gross margin framework (43.6-43.8%) and its raised EPS guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat on adjusted EPS ($0.58) and revenue, stock +4.10%. Q1 2026 EPS miss ($0.37), stock still +4.48%. EPS beats have not been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the company told the market and the whisper sits $0.02 above consensus. If fully priced, the whisper and consensus would already embed it, which they mostly do.
findings.independence: MBI Deep Dives recap of the same call (https://www.mbi-deepdives.com/fnd2q26/, 2026-08-02), which is the same underlying document. Inside guidance, so sized small.

findings.finding: Positioning leans to a squeeze on any non-negative print. Short interest is 13.8m shares (13.0% of shares outstanding, 5.1 days to cover at 2026-10-15). The 25-delta skew is +14.5 vol points with put OI dominant. The stock is down ~23% from early August and ~35% from its 52-week high. FND rose after 6 of its last 7 prints, including after a Q1 miss with a guide cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 7 prints: +4.10, +4.48, +4.34, -3.89, +2.18, +2.51, +1.54 (baseline). The one decline came on a comp at the low end of expectations.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew says the market is paying for downside, the opposite of this lean. The case is that a 13%-short name with put-heavy positioning that has bought its prints six of seven times has a squeeze mechanism the skew does not price.
findings.independence: Baseline skew and reaction history (sealed file); the Earnings Whispers 2026-10-21 preview describes sentiment as 'only mildly bearish' near the bottom of the post-earnings range.

findings.finding: Stifel downgraded FND to Hold on 2026-10-26, citing a less favourable housing outlook, and Wells Fargo cut its target to $45 from $55 around 2026-10-20. Sell-side expectations were being reset lower into the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: public before the print. A lowered bar may even help the reaction. Aggregator only; no primary note found.
findings.independence: Same aggregator for both items; none independent.

findings.finding: Management expects the laminate/vinyl oversupply to pressure average ticket at least through 1H27, with more aggressive pricing where elasticity shows. That is a drag on Q3 ticket (Q2 ticket +0.8%) and on the 2027 framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First disclosed on the Q1/Q2 calls; the stock rose after both.
findings.why_not_priced: Company-disclosed and in the guide ('already reflected in guidance'), so mostly priced. The residual is how it is framed for 2027.
findings.independence: Floordaily trade reporting of SPC/WPC price erosion (https://www.floordaily.net/?p=22375, Feb 2026). Shares the call transcript with the comp-math and refund findings.

findings.finding: Freight and oil inflation: management named rising domestic trucking rates and oil costs as headwinds, and the 43.6-43.8% gross margin framework implies no recovery from Q1's 44.0%. That is a risk to Q3 adjusted gross margin against a framework that leans on tariff refunds.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the company's own framework, so mostly priced.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview flags rising freight and oil (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FND/21195).

findings.finding: Executive Chair Thomas Taylor exercised and sold 218,189 options at $62.30 on 2026-08-07 (about $13.6m), keeping 229,820 shares. It is the only open-market insider sale since the Q2 print, and it was an option exercise.
findings.why_not_priced: Public Form 4 and an option exercise; immaterial.

findings.finding: Mohawk (largest US flooring maker) reports Q3 2026 on the same evening (2026-10-29, call 2026-10-30 11:00 ET). Its Flooring North America read will land inside FND's exit window, direction unknown. Q2 FNA sales were +3.1% reported.
findings.why_not_priced: Not yet released; it adds variance, not direction.

findings.finding: Store openings on plan: a new warehouse store opened in Melbourne, FL on 2026-10-22. 11 stores opened in H1 against 20 planned for FY26, weighted to Q4. No sign of a slowdown in the store programme.

baseline_tension: The negatives (rates, peers) agree with the +14.5 put skew and are largely what drove the 23% drawdown. The small positive lean cuts against the skew, and rests on the company's own comp arithmetic, a 13%-of-shares short and a 6-of-7 up reaction history, so p_up is held at 53 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 / lesson 5: the housing-rates finding is a macro proxy agreeing with the put skew on a 13%-of-shares short, so it shrank from -1.5 to -1.0.
Lesson 2 / lesson 6: the tariff-refund and buyback EPS finding sits inside the company's guide, so it shrank from +1.0 to +0.5.
Lesson 5: the Sherwin-Williams peer proxy shrank from -0.5 to -0.4 because half its own release (pro repaint +MSD) argues the other way.
Lesson 1: the reaction history (6 of 7 up, including after a miss) kept the positioning finding at +1.5 and moved p_up from 52 to 53.
Lesson 3: the comp-math (+) and rates (-) guidance findings were checked as a pair; both can be true (an easy Q4 lap against worsening macro), so both stand at their own sizes.
